name: histogram-slider
title: Histogram slider
description: A range slider over a distribution: bars drawn in CSS behind the track fade outside the chosen range, with minimum and maximum fields.
docs: buckets are the counts of equal parts of the range, from min to max, one bar each. The bars are drawn in CSS behind the track, full strength inside the chosen range and faint outside, cut exactly at the handles, and hidden from assistive technology. The sentence under the heading ("312 homes between 800 and 1,400 euros") carries the information and is read out politely as the handles move: noun gives the singular and plural of what is counted, formatValue writes a value, and summary writes the whole sentence if you say it differently. The count is exact when the handles stand on the edges of the bars and an estimate between them. value and onValueChange work as on any field with a [low, high] pair; onValueCommit fires once when a drag ends or a key press settles. The handles never cross, so the minimum cannot pass the maximum. Each is a slider with a 44px target and takes the arrow keys, the Page keys (ten steps), Home and End; a press anywhere on the track moves the nearest one, and handles that stand together are told apart by the way the pointer goes. The minimum and maximum fields stay in step with the handles, are clamped between the limits and the other end, and read numbers the way the locale writes them ("1,400" or "1.400").
